Baram v0.7.2 — pick the typefaces the editor writes in, turn off the features you
don't use, and export through a stricter gate.

## Fonts

**Settings > Editor > Font** now decides what your documents are written in, and the
body and code faces are set separately.

Two typefaces ship with the app, so a document looks the same on macOS, Windows and
Linux rather than falling back to whatever each machine happens to have:
**Pretendard Variable** for body text and **JetBrains Mono Variable** for code. Both are
under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, and **Baram > About Baram > Bundled fonts** shows
each licence in full.

Click a face's name to open a two-pane browser:

- Families are grouped **Included**, **Recent** and **Installed**, each name drawn in its
  own face — a list of names tells you nothing about how a typeface reads.
- **Search**, plus **Korean** and **Monospace** chips. The code slot starts out
  monospace-only; turning that chip off widens it to everything.
- The right pane previews body and code together, in Latin, Hangul and the glyphs
  typefaces most often disagree about — and carries the same size and line-height
  sliders as the settings rows, because it is one setting seen from two places.
- **Refresh** re-reads your machine's fonts after you install one. If they cannot be
  read at all, it says so and falls back to the bundled families rather than showing an
  empty pane.

A badge on each row says where the face comes from — **Included**, **System**
(**System · Korean** when it covers Hangul), or **Not on this machine**. That last one
matters: a font you don't have still renders through a fallback, so without the badge a
broken choice looks like a working one. You can still type a family name Baram did not
find; it is saved and badged honestly.

**Code size follows body size** unless you say otherwise. **Match Body Text** derives
the code metrics from the body ones at the ratio the stylesheet already used, so the
default is pixel-for-pixel what it was before this release. Turn it off and the two code
sliders become editable; either way they keep showing what your code is actually
rendering at.

**Your choice follows the document out.** HTML and PDF exports name the faces you
picked. PDF always embeds the bundled ones. HTML offers **Embed fonts (+2.7MB)** in the
export dialog, off by default — turn it on when the file has to keep its typeface on a
machine that doesn't have it.

## Features you don't use can go away

Journal, Zettel, Tasks and AI each have an **Enable** toggle at the top of their settings
tab. Turning one off now takes its surfaces with it: its activity-bar icons, its
slash-menu group, its command-palette entries, its right-panel modes, and — for AI —
the ✨ buttons in all three toolbars and on every block that had one. Native menu items
for a disabled feature grey out.

Its keyboard shortcuts stay bound. Pressing one tells you the feature is off rather than
doing nothing, so a shortcut in your muscle memory explains itself instead of appearing
broken.

Settings tabs are grouped now — **General**, **Features**, **System** — and a disabled
feature's tab dims rather than disappearing, so it can always be turned back on.

## OpenRouter

**OpenRouter** joins Claude, OpenAI, Gemini and Ollama in **Settings > AI**. Its model
list loads from your account, and the default is the auto router, which picks the
upstream model for you rather than naming one that may have been retired.

Per-task model choices now survive a change of default provider instead of being reset
by it.

## Exports go through a stricter gate

Pandoc exports (Word, LaTeX, EPUB, RST) are no longer a passthrough for whatever HTML a
note contains.

- **Images are judged three times** — in the editor, at the Rust boundary against the
  canonical path, and finally by a policy filter running inside Pandoc itself on the
  document it actually parsed. Pandoc can read only the images your vault boundary
  allows; anything outside it degrades to its alt text and the count of what was dropped
  is reported rather than being silent.
- **Raw HTML is dropped rather than passed through**, so a `<script>` or a styled `<div>`
  in a note cannot ride into a `.docx`. Subscript, superscript and underline are written
  in Pandoc's own syntax instead, so they survive as formatting rather than as markup.
- Attributes a note can attach to a div, span, header, link or image are scrubbed.

Resized images and cell line breaks survive the export, and a figure keeps its own
caption.

## Fixed

- **Renaming a block ID only changed it in the file you were looking at.** References to
  it elsewhere kept pointing at the old id. A committed rename now lands wherever the
  document lives, and the change is written to the document only after the backend has
  renamed the references — so a failure cannot leave the two disagreeing. Unsaved work in
  a referring tab is kept, and you are warned before a rename touches a file you have
  unsaved edits in.
- **Last session's vault could look gone on launch.** The startup effect runs once and
  read the settings and context stores at mount, but both rehydrate asynchronously from
  storage — so on a cold start or a slow disk it saw empty defaults, took the "nothing to
  restore" path, and locked itself before the real state arrived. The vault came back
  when you reopened it by hand, and until then the link index held a root that was
  registered but never indexed. Startup now waits for both stores, and still proceeds if
  a read fails rather than hanging forever on a corrupt config.
- **Changing a space's directory left its context pointing at the old folder**, and a
  refused move lost the active seat rather than putting it back.
- **The Zettel home note had to be typed as a path.** You can pick it from a file dialog
  now, and the warning about a note outside the Zettel folder is judged by where the file
  is rather than by whether it could be read.
- **Reference-style links** (`[text][ref]`) are rewritten as inline links when you save —
  the documentation now says so instead of leaving you to discover it.
- **The settings nav was part monochrome and part not.** Five tabs drew emoji, and emoji
  carry their own colour. Every tab icon is a monotone glyph now — matched to the icon a
  sibling surface already uses where there is one.

---

**Updating.** Every platform installs in place and restarts — press **Install & Restart**
in the update dialog. Linux `.deb` and `.rpm` cannot be updated in place by the updater;
those, and any install that fails, open the releases page instead.

**Coming from v0.7.0?** The update dialog on that version opens *behind* the Settings
window — that was fixed in v0.7.1, but the app performing an update is the one you are
updating *from*. Press the update button, then click the dimmed area outside the Settings
panel to close Settings; the dialog is waiting there. (Escape closes the dialog rather
than Settings, so use the click.)
